exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong makeover plan defends every gallon and dollar — here is how one student budgeted a garage makeover.

traits.sample: The garage floor is L-shaped, so I cut it into a 10×8 part and a 4×6 part: 80 + 24 = 104 square feet.
traits.why: It shows the decomposition and adds the partial areas clearly.

traits.trait: Rounds paint UP to whole gallons
traits.sample: My walls need 2.3 gallons, but stores sell whole gallons, so I must buy 3 — rounding down would leave a bare wall.
traits.why: It connects the division answer to what you can actually buy.

traits.sample: With a $900 limit I picked the $2 tile over the $4 wood, freeing $208 for better paint — I showed both totals to prove it fits.
traits.why: Strong work compares options with math before choosing.

traits.sample: Two coats means double the wall area: 460 ft² × 2 = 920 ft², which needs 920 ÷ 350 = 2.6, so 3 gallons.
traits.why: The doubling happens to the area first, then the gallons are recomputed.
